stories.headline: Anthony Gordon: Premier League players most fatigued at summer tournaments
stories.summary: Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.
stories.body:
Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.

The inquest into England's painful World Cup semifinal defeat to Argentina continues, with focus on their energy-sapping style of football and inability to keep the ball in the same way that Spain can.

Boss Tuchel said fatigue played a part in their capitulation, coming on the back of extra time in their quarterfinal win against Norway in Miami heat and emotionally-draining victories against Congo DR and Mexico.

Gordon says those playing in the relentlessness of the Premier League are at a disadvantage at the back end of tournaments.

"I think that would probably be a fact," he said. "I don't know the stats, but I think for sure because in England, I'm not saying there is an easy game in any other leagues, but every game is as hard as the next.

"Playing Arsenal is the same as playing a newly-promoted side. That's the difficulty of the Premier League. Every game is so intense. Anyone can win a game.

"I mean, I think Hull, a newly-promoted team, were unbeaten until they played Newcastle.

"So that shows the strength of the Premier League, the strength of the English game, and I think for the English players playing in the Premier League, it would be a lot tougher on the body than players elsewhere."

Gordon's substitution in the semifinal remains a big talking point -- he was withdrawn 16 minutes after putting his side 1-0 up and replaced by a defender.

- Tuchel's England dilemma: Emulate Spain or embrace Premier League 'chaos'?

- Bukayo Saka: 'Tough' to stay on England bench in Argentina World Cup loss

- Harry Kane: Argentina defeat was most painful England moment yet

The game quickly unravelled after that and Gordon said that match needed a lot of unpacking in his personal diary afterwards.

"It was more than one page, I can tell you that," he added. "Maybe not consistently, but I always like to write things down. It just makes you feel more clear.

"I think everyone does that in a different way. Some people use laptops, or some people don't like to do anything.

"My version of that has always been just to write it down, and I kind of like it because I can look back on it and pass it on to my kids.

"But the Argentina game was probably the most memorable one I've had because I didn't really know what to write. I wrote down just pure emotion of what I felt.

"Obviously, I won't go into those details, but it was it was a good few pages, I can tell you."

stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Giants' Nabers trending toward playing Sunday
stories.summary: Giants wideout Malik Nabers is nursing a shoulder injury but says he should be fine for Sunday's game.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 24: Notes from NFL Nation

Giants' Nabers (shoulder) trending in right direction for Sunday

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers practiced for a second straight day Thursday and said he's feeling good and should be fine after injuring a shoulder Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams. Nabers looks like he's trending toward playing Sunday against the Tennessee Titans without any playing-time restrictions. An X-ray earlier in the week on Nabers' injured shoulder didn't reveal any serious problems. "Good results," he said. "I'm smiling. I'm out there playing, catching the ball. So, good results." -- Jordan Raanan

Sept. 23: Need a QB before Week 3? The best reliable, under-the-radar options

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

You couldn't find much more contrast between Weeks 1 and 2 of this NFL season.

A week after the NFL matched the opening-week record for points scored (791), the 32 teams combined to score only 647 in Week 2. Per ESPN Research, the 647 are the fewest points in any non-Week 18 slate since Week 2 of the 2024 season.

Injuries had quite a bit to do with it, particularly at the quarterback position. Through two weeks, we've already seen five starters depart games due to injury, and that excludes the Atlanta Falcons' two combatants for their starting job (Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.) who have yet to play in 2026. Among the quarterbacks expected to be absent for Week 3 are three members of the position's top 10 in terms of ADP (average draft position): Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart and Caleb Williams.

These high-profile injury setbacks have sent many a fantasy manager scrambling to find a quality quarterback, and there are plenty of options out there to be had -- standard, Knockout, Vampire, etc., leagues alike. Three in particular stand out, players who went 17th or later at the position in the preseason but are suddenly viable starters:

Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints: His Consistency Ratings won't reflect it due to his initial backup status to begin last season, but if we splice Shough's results into the games he started versus served in a backup capacity, he has been remarkably reliable. He's one of five quarterbacks to score 20-plus fantasy points in each of 2026's first two weeks, finishing eighth in scoring at the position in each, and he has been a top-10 scorer in five of his past seven starts.

Shough still has inconsistencies, especially with how deliberate he has been with his throws early in those games (not to mention taking too many sacks), but the mettle he has shown while leading his team to an overtime loss and a win over the Baltimore Ravens speaks highly for his future potential. Shough is already in my top 10 rankings for Week 3 (LV) -- he was my must-get in our staff Vampire league -- and he has a good matchup for Week 4 (ATL), too.

Shough, incidentally, leads all quarterbacks in expected fantasy points, yet he's still out there in 32.1% of ESPN leagues.

Jared Goff, Detroit Lions: The one of these three who wasn't out there in any of our staff leagues, Goff was the QB17 in terms of ADP during the preseason, despite the high-octane offense he leads and the supremely favorable schedule his team faces in 2026. He's fourth on the aforementioned expected fantasy points list, and he turned in a top-10 weekly quarterback score in 42% of his games since the beginning of 2024. While unfortunately unavailable in any of our staff leagues, Goff was a clear QB2 target of mine in my home two-quarterback league, and he's still out there in 24.9% of ESPN leagues.

Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers: Admittedly, it's tough to rely on a quarterback who in only six of his 30 starts in 2024-25 combined earned a place in your fantasy lineup -- meaning a top-10 weekly positional score -- with five of those coming across the season's final eight weeks. But Young looks like a decidedly different player this year, particularly his improvements on deep throws. On attempts of 10 air yards or greater, he has completed 68% of his passes, more than 23% better than his career rate entering 2026 and been off-target on only 24%, down 11%. At the very least, Young is now a streaming option, and he has a good Week 3 matchup in the Cleveland Browns. He's also out there in 40.4% of ESPN leagues.

Sept. 23: RB Brooks out for at least six weeks

Jonathon Brooks is set to miss at least six weeks after undergoing core muscle surgery, leaving Chuba Hubbard as the undisputed No. 1 in Carolina's backfield with AJ Dillon as the backup.

In this week's Facts vs. Feelings, Liz Loza pointed out that Hubbard finished as fantasy's RB10 in both Week 1 and Week 2, commanding Carolina's backfield with 27 touches for 151 scrimmage yards and three total touchdowns.

She was already treating Hubbard as a low-tier RB 2 for his matchup against the Browns.

NFL Nation's Mike Kaye reports that the Panthers will bring in Austin Ekeler for a workout. At this point it is too early to make a speculative add in anything but the deepest of formats.

Sept. 22: Giants take a hit with loss of Jaxson Dart, uncertainty around Bears starting QB

By Michael F. Florio

Adam Schefter reported Tuesday that tests revealed that Jaxson Dart's knee injury is worse than initially thought, and the QB is now facing the possibility of season-ending surgery. Dart missing the season would be a crushing blow for the fantasy stock of Giants players.

Jameis Winston is the next man up. While that has meant good things for his receivers in the past, he looked rough Monday night. Given his past tendencies to lock in and pepper his top receiver with targets, Malik Nabers still has fantasy hope. While this news drops Nabers into more of the WR2 range for the rest of the season, he still brings upside given his immense talent ... just expect more weekly volatility as well. If Nabers managers are panicking after his 1.1 fantasy points Monday with Winston under center, it could be a good time to buy low.

Isaiah Likely remains a TE1, though his fantasy ceiling does take a hit here (Likely was targeted nine times by Winston for a 33% target share). While this news could mean the Giants become a more run-heavy offense, that would help keep Cam Skattebo afloat. His fantasy value still takes a slight hit as there will be less consistent scoring chances without Dart, but he should see enough volume to remain in the low-end RB2 range.

Some QBs managers can look to add to replace Dart in one-QB leagues are Kyler Murray, Tyler Shough, Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud. As for Winston, he is purely an option for superflex leagues and is more of a depth QB3 than a starter.

Bears' starting QB up in the air for Week 3

Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol, and his status is up in the air for Week 3. With Caleb Williams dealing with a hamstring injury, that would leave veteran Case Keenum as the starter for the Chicago Bears. To make matters trickier, the Bears play on "Monday Night Football," so fantasy managers will have to decide what to do with their Bears players on Sunday, potentially without knowing who will be starting at QB.

For those looking to replace Williams, the options to replace Dart (Murray, Shough, Young and Stroud) are good options here, too. For those in superflex, your options are more limited, as you can add Marcus Mariota or Winston.

The bigger fantasy question is what should fantasy managers do with their Bears in a tough matchup against the Eagles? D'Andre Swift, who has seen safe volume as a runner and receiver, is the Bear you can start with the most confidence. Kyle Monangai would be a flex option who could see a boost in volume, as the Bears likely would try to run more than usual. Last season against Philly, Swift ran for 125 yards and a touchdown, adding in a 13-yard catch. Monangai ran for 130 yards and a touchdown.

The Bears' pass catchers have been disappointing to start the season, and in this matchup, with potentially a third-string QB, none are must-starts. Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III are both outside the top 30 WRs in ESPN consensus Week 3 rankings and should be viewed as "boom or bust" flex options.

Colston Loveland has been the biggest fantasy disappointment on the Bears to start the season. Through two games, he has just one catch for 3 yards (the third-most yards among Bears TEs). On top of that, the Eagles have allowed the second-fewest yards to tight ends this season, after allowing the second-fewest yards to the position in 2025. Some tight ends I would play over him are Dalton Kincaid, George Kittle, Isaiah Likely, Tucker Kraft, Dalton Schultz and Terrance Ferguson.

Falcons pledge to get TE Pitts more involved

By Marc Raimondi

Kyle Pitts Sr. has just one catch through two games. Fantasy football team managers want more. So does Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator and playcaller Tommy Rees.

"We've gotta get it going," Rees said Tuesday when asked about the tight end. "That's my job. He's an integral part of what we want to do."

The return of Michael Penix Jr. should be a boon for those who have Pitts on their fantasy teams. Penix will return from left ACL surgery to start Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers.

Pitts had 88 receptions for 928 yards last season, trailing only Trey McBride in both categories at the position. Quarterback play has been an issue this season. Third-stringer Cooper Rush had Total QBRs of 2.6 and 5.2, respectively, the first two weeks of the season, the worst marks in the league.

Notes from "Monday Night Football"

By Michael F. Florio

The Rams looked like the Rams again on "Monday Night Football". Matthew Stafford played like an MVP, throwing for 327 yards, four touchdowns and one interception. He is a QB1 most weeks, but with the Denver Broncos on tap next week, he is a little more option-dependent.
Wide receiver Davante Adams was the star of the night with Puka Nacua sidelined. Adams caught eight of 10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The future Hall of Famer is in play weekly, but he is a must-start any time Nacua is out.
Both of the Rams' RBs balled out. Kyren Williams played 55% of snaps, with 12 carries, 14 routes and two targets, turning that work into 97 yards and a touchdown. Blake Corum played 45% of snaps, with 12 carries, seven routes, one target and 92 scrimmage yards. Williams is sharing more carries than in the past, but his red zone and pass-game usage keeps him in play as a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2. He has a very safe floor and clear upside. Corum is a high-upside flex option.
Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson will be a popular name on the waiver wire this week. He saw nine targets, second on the team, and caught six of them for 54 yards and a touchdown. There were a couple of just-missed, big-play opportunities as well. Ferguson has breakout upside in one of the league's best offenses.
While he is not a fantasy piece, Aaron Donald's return for the Rams was notable as well. Seeing his first action since his return from retirement, the defensive tackle played 58% of the snaps, producing one QB pressure and one run stuff. He drew seven double-teams, the most of anyone on the Rams defensive line. The big fella is back, and he's still got it.
Malachi Fields saw six targets and continues to operate as the WR2 for the Giants. While fantasy managers should not trust him with Winston, they should keep an eye on him once Dart returns.

Sept. 21: Nacua ruled out for 'Monday Night Football'

By Michael F. Florio

Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua has been ruled out for "Monday Night Football" because of a hip injury. That leaves Davante Adams as the top target for Matthew Stafford against the New York Giants.

For those fantasy managers who rolled the dice on Nacua's availability, replacement options are Malachi Fields, Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Darnell Mooney. For those who left him in the flex spot, Terrance Ferguson is an upside option whom I would use over all those receivers except Fields. If you have Blake Corum available to plug in as your flex, he is the top option.

Sept. 21: Kyler Murray clears protocol, will start Week 3

By Michael F. Florio

Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We have not seen much of Murray in a Vikings uniform, but he brings QB1 upside due to his rushing ability and the matchup.

The Bucs have allowed 234 passing yards per game, which ranks 11th highest in the NFL. That is after allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the NFL in 2025. Last week they allowed 19.72 fantasy points to Deshaun Watson, 11th-best among QBs through Sunday.

Murray was a fantasy target of mine this summer due to him being in the best system of his career, with great pass catchers around him. He has been top 12 in fantasy points per game among QBs in every year but one of his career. That is largely due to his rushing ability and highlights the safe floor he brings.

Some QBs I would start him over in Week 3 are Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Baker Mayfield and Jordan Love.

Which Commanders should you start with Daniels out?

Marcus Mariota is expected to start Week 3 for the Washington Commanders as Jayden Daniels continues to seek opinions on his dislocated left elbow. Daniels does not have a timetable as of now.

Mariota started eight games for the Commanders last season, averaging 200 passing yards and 32 rushing yards per game. He threw 10 touchdowns and added another with his legs.

Mariota is not someone fantasy managers should be looking to force into their lineups. He is more an option for those in superflex leagues who now find themselves in a pinch. He brings a safer floor than you might expect, thanks to the rushing numbers, but falls far short of Daniels' ceiling.

Washington faces the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, so even those in superflex leagues should look in another direction to help replace Daniels in their starting lineup. I would also recommend trying to avoid the Commanders' pass catchers in this one. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs remain the team's top options, but they are more "boom-or-bust" WR3 or flex plays.

Mariota did throw four times each to McLaurin and Dyami Brown in Week 2. He threw three times to Diggs, but the duo did connect for a touchdown.

Dallas Goedert to miss time

Goedert suffered a sprained MCL and is expected to miss a few weeks, per Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. Goedert exited early in Week 2, playing only 26% of the snaps.

Goedert was the go-to receiving option in the red zone for the Eagles, evident by his two Week 1 touchdowns. The Philadelphia tight ends room is very thin at the moment with rookie Eli Stowers on injured reserve. That likely leads to an uptick in targets for the Eagles' receivers. Dontayvion Wicks should be added off waivers. Makai Lemon remains an upside stash.

Dalton Schultz, Juwan Johnson, Darren Waller and Oronde Gadsden are tight ends fantasy managers in need can look to add off the waiver wire.

Sept. 21: Who got the ball Sunday?

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons

Chuba Hubbard led the Panthers' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (14), finishing with 14.4 fantasy points. Carolina used more of a committee approach with Jonathon Brooks before he left in the fourth quarter with a groin injury and didn't return. If Brooks is ruled out, Hubbard can be viewed as a midrange RB2 against the Browns.

Kyle Pitts Sr. remains in a tight end rotation with Austin Hooper and Charlie Woerner. Pitts saw just three targets and finished with 2.5 fantasy points, although the Falcons did pull their starters for the final 13 plays. Pitts' reduced playing time, particularly in 11 personnel, remains a concern. Cooper Rush's struggles also limited the entire offense. Pitts moves back into TE1 consideration if Michael Penix Jr. returns in Week 3 but is difficult to trust if Rush starts again.

Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears

Aaron Jones Sr. led the Vikings' backfield in snaps and carries (23), rushing for 105 yards against the Bears. With Jordan Mason on injured reserve and wet, windy conditions limiting the passing game, Minnesota leaned heavily on Jones. He wasn't targeted but recorded his first 100-yard rushing performance since 2024. Jones suffered a knee injury in the second half but played through it. His health is worth monitoring, but he's firmly on the RB2 radar against the Buccaneers in Week 3 if active.

Rome Odunze led the Bears' receivers in snaps (62) and routes (38), while Luther Burden III played 42 snaps and ran 30 routes. Colston Loveland played 64 snaps but ran just 29 routes as he was asked to pass block more often. Burden's playing time remains a concern, while Loveland's limited route participation hurts his upside. Caleb Williams' hamstring injury could further limit all three players if Tyson Bagent starts against the Eagles in Week 3.

D'Andre Swift led the Bears' backfield in snaps and touches (21), finishing with 12.9 fantasy points against the Vikings. Kyle Monangai played fewer snaps and had 12 touches, rushing for a team-high 47 yards. Swift also lost a costly fumble at the goal line. The backfield remains a committee, but Swift has the edge in playing time and receiving opportunities, leading the way in snaps, routes and targets. Both backs could see more work in Week 3 if Williams misses time with his hamstring injury.

Philadelphia Eagles at Tennessee Titans

Saquon Barkley missed significant time after suffering a stinger in the first quarter but returned for the second half. Tank Bigsby handled most of the early-down work in his absence, while Will Shipley took on more passing down snaps. Bigsby finished with 15 touches and 11.8 fantasy points. He's the Eagles' insurance back to roster and would have league-winning upside in this offense if Barkley misses extended time.

Pittsburgh Steelers at New England Patriots

Jaylen Warren played a career-high number of snaps against the Patriots and dominated the Steelers' backfield after Rico Dowdle left with a toe injury in the second quarter. Warren has averaged 4.7 yards per carry and 7.3 yards per reception in his career but has rarely had the backfield to himself. In six career games with at least a 60% snap share, he has averaged 13.0 fantasy points. He has also averaged 14.4 fantasy points in 19 games with at least 15 touches. Warren's fantasy upside increases significantly if Dowdle misses time.

DK Metcalf led the Steelers' skill-position players in snaps, routes and targets against the Patriots, but he caught just four passes and finished with 8.0 fantasy points. He also had two drops. His 19 targets and 44.7% share of Pittsburgh's air yards this season are encouraging, but his 42.1% catch rate needs to improve. Metcalf has scored just 14.7 fantasy points through two games, far from the start fantasy managers were hoping for. He's best viewed as a low-end flex option heading into Week 3.

Hunter Henry, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins led the Patriots in routes but combined for just 10 targets, with Henry and Doubs seeing four apiece. Drake Maye and the passing game continue to struggle through two games. Doubs finished with 12.6 fantasy points and remains the Patriots receiver to roster with A.J. Brown on injured reserve, even as Maye continues to spread the targets around. Doubs is still best viewed as a flex option in deeper leagues.

TreVeyon Henderson led the Patriots' backfield in snaps, routes run and carries (16), finishing with 13.6 fantasy points thanks in part to a 39-yard touchdown run. He capitalized on an early fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson and now has five rushing touchdowns of at least 30 yards since the start of last season, the most in the league. Henderson can be viewed as a low-end RB2 against the Jaguars in Week 3.

Green Bay Packers at New York Jets

The Packers used a three-man backfield with Josh Jacobs still out. Kaleb Johnson led the team with eight carries, while MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks split the remaining work. Brooks dominated passing situations, while Lloyd led the way with 8.6 fantasy points but lost a fumble in the fourth quarter. All three remain difficult to trust in fantasy lineups.

Tucker Kraft played nearly every snap against the Jets and appears to have no playing time restrictions. He ran nearly as many routes as Christian Watson and Matthew Golden but saw just three targets. If Jayden Reed misses Week 3 due to injury, Watson, Golden and Kraft should see additional targets in Green Bay's passing game.

Cleveland Browns at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Bucky Irving led the Buccaneers' backfield in early down, third down and short-yardage snaps, finishing with 21 touches and 13.0 fantasy points. Kenny Gainwell managed just five touches and 4.5 fantasy points. Irving has taken control of this backfield and is firmly on the RB2 radar. Gainwell is merely an insurance back with little standalone fantasy value.

Quinshon Judkins led the Browns' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (17) following Dylan Sampson's placement on injured reserve. Judkins finished with 9.8 fantasy points as Cleveland's running game struggled, managing just 44 yards at 1.9 yards per carry. Despite the poor production, Judkins' workload keeps him firmly on the RB2 radar.

New Orleans Saints at Baltimore Ravens

Alvin Kamara finished with 14 touches but managed just 22 yards against the Ravens. Travis Etienne Jr. led the backfield in snaps, while CJ Donaldson maintained his third-down role. Kamara dominated the touches early, but Etienne saw more work in the second half. The committee approach and lack of production make both backs difficult to trust. Kamara is a desperation flex option against the Raiders in Week 3, while Etienne is a low-end RB2.

Juwan Johnson caught all four of his targets for 66 yards against the Ravens, but his playing time raises concerns. With Oscar Delp returning, the Saints used more of a tight end rotation involving Johnson and Noah Fant. Johnson's route participation dropped significantly from Week 1 to Week 2, making his production difficult to sustain. He's best viewed as a TE2 against the Raiders in Week 3.

Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans

David Montgomery and Woody Marks split snaps fairly evenly in the Texans' backfield against the Bengals. Montgomery managed just 4.4 fantasy points on eight touches after scoring 28.9 fantasy points in Week 1. Marks finished with 8.5 fantasy points on 13 touches, including five receptions. Houston continues to rotate backs by drive, limiting both players' fantasy ceilings. Montgomery remains on the RB2 radar against the Colts in Week 3, while Marks is a flex option.

Jacksonville Jaguars at Denver Broncos

J.K. Dobbins suffered a hamstring injury late in the third quarter and didn't return, opening the door for Jonah Coleman with RJ Harvey already sidelined. Coleman led the Broncos' backfield in snaps and touches (13), finishing with 14.8 fantasy points. He handled early downs after Dobbins exited, while Tyler Badie took passing-down work. Coleman is a priority waiver wire pickup and could have RB2 upside against the Rams if Dobbins and Harvey are out.

Bhayshul Tuten led the Jaguars' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (15), finishing with 14.2 fantasy points. His usage compared with Chris Rodriguez Jr. was notable. We'll see if that trend continues in Week 3. Tuten is firmly on the RB2 radar against the Patriots in Week 3.

Washington Commanders at Dallas Cowboys

Jake Ferguson caught all four targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns against the Commanders, but his usage is concerning. He played just 60% of snaps and ranked fourth in routes and targets behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Reduced playing time and increased target competition make Ferguson more touchdown-dependent. He's a TE2 against the Ravens in Week 3, and now is a good time to explore his trade value.

Las Vegas Raiders at Los Angeles Chargers

Omarion Hampton led the Chargers' backfield in snaps and touches (25), finishing with 17.5 fantasy points against the Raiders. Keaton Mitchell saw six touches, while Kimani Vidal became more involved on third downs. Despite the three-man rotation, Hampton continues to dominate the workload, but his second lost fumble in two games is concerning. He remains firmly on the RB2 radar against the Bills in Week 3.

Seattle Seahawks at Arizona Cardinals

Marvin Harrison Jr. played the third-most snaps and tied Trey McBride for the second-most routes among Cardinals pass catchers, but he finished without a catch on one target. He has just four targets and one reception through two games. His snap share has also declined, with Michael Wilson seeing more work in single receiver sets. McBride continues to dominate targets, leaving Harrison difficult to trust. He's a boom-or-bust flex option against the 49ers in Week 3.

Miami Dolphins at San Francisco 49ers

George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins. He's still working his way back from an Achilles injury, but his route participation increased from Week 1 to Week 2 as the 49ers used him more in passing situations. Kittle's playing time remains limited as he continues to split snaps with Luke Farrell and Brayden Willis, but his increased involvement in the passing game is encouraging. He remains on the TE1 radar against the Cardinals in Week 3.

Indianapolis Colts at Kansas City Chiefs

Rashee Rice caught four of six targets for 83 yards against the Colts, but his role in Kansas City's offense has changed. He's spending less time in the slot, while Xavier Worthy is earning targets at a higher rate. Travis Kelce (17) and Kenneth Walker III (16) lead the team in targets through two games, with Walker seeing more opportunities on shorter passes. Rice remains on the WR2 radar with Patrick Mahomes under center, but his changing usage and increased target competition are concerning.

stories.headline: Cubs earn second straight playoff berth with win over Marlins
stories.summary: The Chicago Cubs clinched their second straight postseason berth a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- Pete Crow-Armstrong joined the 40-40 club by stealing his 40th base to go along with his major-league-leading 45 home runs, and the Chicago Cubs clinched their second straight postseason berth a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins on Thursday.

Seiya Suzuki homered for the Cubs (88-71), who assured themselves of one of the NL's three wild-card berths.

Chicago also was a wild card last year when the Cubs beat San Diego in the first round and lost to Milwaukee in a division series. The Cubs will be making consecutive postseason appearances for the first time since four straight from 2015 to 2018, which in 2016 included their first championship since 1908.

The Cubs clinched their berth shortly after the White Sox earned their postseason trip with a 9-1 win at Kansas City.

It was the first time the White Sox and Cubs clinched playoff berths on the same day, according to ESPN Research. It's only the fourth year both Chicago teams reached the postseason. The others were the COVID-shortened 2020 season, 2008 and 1906.

Miami (78-81) was assured its third straight non-winning season.

A favorite to win the NL MVP award, Crow-Armstrong became the seventh 40-40 player, joining a group that includes Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani and Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. Jose Canseco was the first with the 1988 Oakland Athletics.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, hit his 45th homer during Sunday's 9-1 win at Cincinnati, extending his career high. He drew a leadoff walk from Tyler Phillips in the first inning and swiped second base on the next pitch to Suzuki for his 40th steal in 47 attempts. Fans chanted "MVP" as the Wrigley Field videoboard proclaimed the feat.

Ohtani was the previous player with a 40-40 season, hitting 54 homers and stealing 59 bases for the 2024 Dodgers. Acuña hit 41 homers and swiped 73 bases for Atlanta in 2023. Alfonso Soriano (2006 with Washington), Alex Rodriguez (1998 with Seattle) and Barry Bonds (1996 with San Francisco) are the other 40-40 players.

Matthew Boyd (10-5) allowed one run, five hits and two walks over seven innings, and Ryan Zeferjahn pitched a perfect ninth for his seventh save to finish a five-hitter.

Ian Happ tripled off Jack Ralston (0-2) to start the sixth and came home three pitches later on Nico Hoerner's single, breaking a 1-1 tie.

Miami's Jakob Marsee had an RBI single in the third and Suzuki hit his 26th homer in the fifth, a drive off Ralston.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Blue Jackets re-sign Adam Fantilli to 6-year, $82.5M deal
stories.summary: The Blue Jackets re-signed center Adam Fantilli to a six-year, $82.5 million contract.
stories.body:
COLUMBUS, Ohio -- The Blue Jackets re-signed center Adam Fantilli to a six-year, $82.5 million contract on Thursday.

Fantilli was a restricted free agent and missed the first week of training camp as the two sides worked on a deal. He becomes the Blue Jackets' highest-paid player with a contract that averages $13.75 million per year.

The 21-year-old Canadian was the third overall pick by Columbus in the 2023 NHL draft after winning the Hobey Baker Award as the top player in college hockey at the University of Michigan.

Fantilli was second on the team with 24 goals and was third in scoring with 59 points last season. He is the third player in franchise history with multiple 20-goal campaigns before turning 22.

"Adam Fantilli has all of the tools you look for in a player -- speed, size, skill -- along with a competitive drive to succeed," general manager Don Waddell said in a statement. "He is one of the most exciting young players in the NHL and a big part of what we are building in Columbus, so this is a very exciting day for our organization and our fans."

Chicago's Connor Bedard and Anaheim's Leo Carlsson -- the top two picks in the 2023 draft -- both signed five-year contracts. Bedard's averages $15 million while the Ducks matched an offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers that had an average of $18 million per season.

San Jose's Will Smith was picked fourth overall but remains on the final year of his entry-level contract.

Fantilli is expected to center Columbus' top line with Kirill Marchenko and Valeri Nichushkin. Marchenko led the Blue Jackets with 27 goals while Nichushkin was acquired from Colorado during the offseason.

Defenseman and reigning Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski has two years remaining on his contract as the Blue Jackets look to get to the playoffs for the first time since 2020.

stories.headline: Fantasy women's hoops: Breakouts, surprises and more tips to remember for next year
stories.summary: Plan ahead to 2027 with the top 10 things to remember from a WNBA season full of fantasy breakouts.
stories.body:
The 2026 WNBA regular season gave fantasy managers plenty to remember before next year's drafts. Several players broke out, young stars took another step forward and offseason moves changed fantasy value in a big way.

By the time 2027 draft season arrives, some of those lessons will be easy to forget. Here are 10 things worth keeping in mind for next season.

Did you enjoy ESPN fantasy women's basketball all season long? Try out ESPN fantasy hockey next and draft your team today!

Olivia Miles has become a fantasy superstar

Miles has exceeded expectations in her rookie season. She has averaged 19.8 PPG, 4.7 RPG, 6.0 APG and 1.3 SPG while posting a team-high 26.5% usage rate among players who appeared in at least 10 games. Miles is currently a top-10 player in fantasy hoops, averaging 35.8 fantasy points per game and outperforming her Round 4 average draft position. She also recently broke Caitlin Clark's rookie scoring record. The odds-on favorite for 2026 Rookie of the Year should be a top-10 pick in in 2027.

Jessica Shepard's breakout looks sustainable

Shepard enjoyed a breakout season with the Dallas Wings, with averages of 14.3 points and 11.1 rebounds while earning her first All-Star selection. She finished as a top-15 fantasy option and joined Candace Parker as the only players in WNBA history to average at least 14 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a season. Shepard also tied for the league lead with five triple-doubles while helping Dallas reach the playoffs. She was available near the end of many drafts and ultimately became a league-winner because of her production.

Dominique Malonga could make another leap

Malonga took a huge step forward in her second season, tallying 17.1 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.4 blocks, 1.0 steals and 33.0 fantasy points per game while earning her first All-Star selection. She also became the youngest player in league history to reach 500 career rebounds. At just 20 years old, Malonga already offers strong scoring, rebounding and defensive production. Another jump in 2027 could push her firmly into the early-round fantasy conversation.

Shakira Austin has finally put everything together

Austin averaged 17.2 PPG, 9.5 RPG and 1.3 BPG with 20 double-doubles this season while helping Washington return to the playoffs. She finished as a top-12 fantasy player at 33.7 fantasy points per game after being a mid-round draft value. Most encouragingly, Austin's usage declined from 28.3% to 26.0% while her production soared. That makes her breakout season look sustainable entering 2027.

Angel Reese's fantasy ceiling goes beyond rebounding

Reese took a major step forward in 2026, averaging 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds while shooting 45.1% from the field. She also set a WNBA single-season record with 32 double-doubles and became the first player in league history with 500 rebounds in a season. For 2027, fantasy managers shouldn't view Reese as just a rebounding specialist. Her improving scoring efficiency and defensive production give her an even higher fantasy ceiling. Only A'ja Wilson, Clark and Breanna Stewart averaged more fantasy points per game this season.

Leila Lacan grows across the board

Lacan continued to expand her role in 2026, increasing her games started from 15 to 29, minutes from 26.6 to 28.4 per game, scoring from 10.4 to 11.7 PPG and assists from 3.7 to 4.5 APG. Her 3-point percentage also leaped from .224 to .327, a significant increase. For 2027, fantasy managers should keep tracking young players whose roles and offensive responsibilities are still growing.

Azzi Fudd could be a strong bounce-back target in 2027

Don't forget how good she was before the injury. Fudd averaged 13.1 points, 2.1 3-pointers, 1.7 steals and 0.8 blocks in 30 games before season-ending right knee surgery. More importantly, she led all rookies in threes, steals and blocks per game while shooting 39.7% from deep. If healthy, that multi-category production could make the 2026 No. 1 WNBA draft pick an intriguing 2027 fantasy target.

The offseason can create some of the biggest fantasy risers

The offseason can completely reshape fantasy value. Shepard became a full-time starter after signing with the Wings and set career highs across the board. Marina Mabrey went from 14.4 PPG with the Connecticut Sun in 2025 to 20.8 with the Toronto Tempo, while Carla Leite jumped from 7.2 PPG and 2.0 APG to 15.9 PPG and 6.3 APG after landing with the Portland Fire. Gabby Williams also increased her scoring from 11.6 PPG to 14.4 after signing with the Golden State Valkyries. For 2027, don't simply carry over your final rankings. Track roster movement, depth charts, projected minutes and usage.

Rickea Jackson could be one of 2027's biggest draft day values

Jackson tore her left ACL on May 17 and missed the rest of the season, so her recovery will be worth watching closely next spring. Her preseason workload and how she looks physically could swing her draft value quite a bit. If she's healthy and close to full strength, Jackson (who was drafted in the sixth round this past season) could become one of the better values in fantasy drafts.

Sonia Citron showed how much a young player can grow in Year 2

Don't assume a strong rookie season is the ceiling. Citron followed an impressive rookie year by increasing her scoring from 14.9 to 16.7 PPG and her assists from 2.4 to 4.4 APG, despite only a slight increase in minutes. She also got to the line much more often, upping her free throws per game from 3.4 to 5.4. For 2027, remember that young players can make significant fantasy jumps even without a major change in playing time.

stories.headline: Lachie Neale ban overturned, free to play AFL Grand Final
stories.summary: Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL grand final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.
stories.body:
Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL Grand Final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.

The dual Brownlow Medal winner will feature in the premiership decider against Fremantle - his former club - at the MCG on Saturday after having a striking charge on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan downgraded on Thursday.

Neale will instead be fined $10,000.

He initially failed in challenging the one-game ban from the match review officer at the tribunal on Tuesday night.

To succeed on appeal, Brisbane had to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

The Lons were able to sway the appeals board that the tribunal had made an error of law in not considering the exceptional and compelling circumstances of Neale not having previously been suspended in 320 AFL games.

Neale avoids becoming the first player to miss an AFL grand final following a preliminary-final suspension since Collingwood's Anthony Rocca in 2003.

Brisbane legal representative Adrian Anderson tried various different arguments to clear Neale.

One included suggesting the ban should be served in round one next year, instead of in the grand final, due to the added importance of the match.

It was a bold strategy given Neale is almost certain to leave Brisbane and join Collingwood during the off-season.

Anderson leaned heavily on Neale's prior record of not being suspended, referring to the four-time All-Australian as "pretty close to a unicorn".

Introduced this year, the "exceptional and compelling circumstances" clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and AFL games record-holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

New vision of Neale's strike on Ginnivan became available on Thursday, but was not allowed to be used because it was not shown at Tuesday's tribunal hearing.

The footage would have shown a clearer picture of the incident and likely not helped Neale's case.

Sydney's Barry Hall (2005) and Richmond's Trent Cotchin (2017) famously escaped bans for incidents in their respective preliminary finals to play in eventual premiership wins.

The Lions named Neale in their team on Thursday, shortly before the decision was handed down, and didn't need to change the 23.

With rain expected for Saturday's grand final, Neale will figure prominently as one of the Lions' best wet-weather players.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Selwyn Cobbo named Queensland's best for State of Origin
stories.summary: Queensland winger Selwyn Cobbo justified his State of Origin recall by winning the Ron McAuliffe Medal at the QRL awards night.
stories.body:
Dolphins winger Selwyn Cobbo received a boost ahead of the NRL preliminary final after winning Queensland's best player award for the State of Origin series.

The 24-year-old scored four tries, made four line breaks and averaged a stunning 184m across the three matches of 2-1 series loss. He was recalled by coach Billy Slater after a two-year absence from the Origin arena, due to the stellar club form he has displayed for the Dolphins.

Cobbo was a worthy winner of the Ron McAuliffe Medal, named in honour of the former senator and influential boss of the Queensland Rugby League.

Cobbo will play against the Sydney Roosters in the grand final qualifier on Friday night.

He won the Queensland gong at the QRL season awards on Thursday night in Brisbane, 17 years after Maroons legend Greg Inglis, who was his idol growing up.

Maroons prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui took out the FOGS Peter Jackson Memorial Award after his brave and emotional display in game two in Melbourne, where he played his heart out just days after his father Fereti Fa'asuamaleaui had died.

The Maroons won the match 44-24.

The award, named in honour of late Queensland star Jackson, is presented to a Maroons player or one of the support staff who epitomises what the Queensland Origin spirit is all about

Cobbo moved to the Dolphins from Brisbane this year and has had a career-best season under head coach Kristian Woolf.

He took on board advice from Maroons coach Slater, who gave him his debut in 2022.

"I'd been there in Origin for a couple of years but didn't play last year, which wasn't the best year for me," Cobbo said.

"I wanted to get back, so I worked really hard the whole off-season. All the extras I was doing paid off.

"As Billy says, if you work hard for it the rewards will come. He was real good throughout the camps, the staff as well.

"Just knowing I can play 80 minutes of Origin was a shock to me, but I enjoyed every moment of it."

Cobbo recently re-signed with the Dolphins until the end of 2031 after finding his feet following a disappointing 2025 at the Broncos.

"The club has done a lot for me. They told me they would bring me back to Origin, and I just want to give back to them and play good footy here for the next five years," he said.

Cobbo's fierce ball running in Origin this year would have made Inglis proud.

"He was my idol growing up, the way he played ... strong. It would have been hard defending against him," Cobbo said.

Now Cobbo is on track to cap off a great season with a recall to the Australian side under his old club coach Kevin Walters at the World Cup, which is another goal.

"It would be good to chuck on that (Australian) jersey again and play under Kevvie. I'll work hard to get back there," he said.

stories.headline: Former England forward Andy Carroll says he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021
stories.summary: Former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.
stories.body:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has said in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.

The 37-year-old included the details in his book, titled "Owning It." As a victim of sexual assault, Carroll was automatically granted anonymity.

Carroll said the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender -- a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time -- was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

Former Liverpool and West Ham striker Carroll, who is now a player/co-owner of National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He said he then threw the man out of the house, and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous."

The 37-year-old said: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

stories.headline: Eagles look to add to perfect start by stopping the Bears' rushing attack on Monday night
stories.summary: — The Chicago Bears made a memorable trip to Philadelphia in November, rushing for 281 yards in an impressive 24-15 victory over the Eagles.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — The Chicago Bears made a memorable trip to Philadelphia in November, rushing for 281 yards in an impressive 24-15 victory over the Eagles.


Philadelphia is hoping to return the favor on Monday night, when it visits Chicago in search of a second straight road win.


“They are one of the better running teams in the league,” Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said. “They’ve got a really great (offensive line), great backs. Their scheme is good. We’re going to have to play it a whole lot better.”


It would be difficult to play it any worse than they did in their matchup last season. D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both went over 100 yards rushing as Chicago possessed the ball for almost 40 minutes in its fifth consecutive victory — a streak that helped propel the Bears to the NFC North title. Philadelphia gained just 87 yards on the ground in the loss.


Swift and Monangai led the way again as Chicago rushed for 291 yards in this year's season opener at Carolina on Sept. 13. But the Bears' ground game was held in check during Sunday's 9-3 loss to Minnesota, finishing with 134 yards on 31 attempts.


Chicago has an uncertain situation at quarterback with Caleb Williams dealing with a right hamstring injury and Tyson Bagent in the concussion protocol. But Fangio doesn't think it will have much of an effect on the Bears' rushing scheme.


“They’re an under-center offense a good bit, so it’s not like it’s a lot of gun zone-read, QB-generated runs,” Fangio said. “They’re under center, handing it off. They do a great job of blocking.”


Philadelphia is coming off a dramatic 24-20 victory at Tennessee. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with 9 seconds left.


“It’s a really good team coming in. ... They make it really difficult for you and it’s sound, both sides of the ball,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “Special teams a good unit as well, so we’ll have our work cut out for us.”


If Williams and Bagent are unable to play, Case Keenum is expected to start for Chicago. The 38-year-old Keenum has made 66 starts in 80 career games, but he hasn’t thrown a pass in a regular-season game since Dec. 24, 2023, for Houston against Cleveland.


“I feel really good,” Keenum said. “There have been some things every year. I call it a little puzzle of trying to figure out how to get your body in the best shape that it can. This year worked a little more on my diet and what I put in, what I fuel it with. Which is not as fun, it’s just boring, but it does help. So, I feel great.”


Need to know
Philadelphia (2-0) at Chicago (1-1).


When/where to watch: Monday, 8:15 p.m. EDT, ESPN/ABC.


Latest odds: Eagles by 4 1/2.


Against the spread: Eagles 0-2, Bears 1-1.


Last week: Eagles beat the Titans 24-20; Bears lost to the Vikings 9-3.


Last meeting: Bears beat Eagles 24-15 on Nov. 28 in Philadelphia.


Series record: Bears lead 30-17-1.


Matchup to watch
Eagles DT Jordan Davis vs. Bears C Garrett Bradbury. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 336 pounds, the 26-year-old Davis presents a sizeable challenge for Bradbury and the rest of Chicago's interior offensive line. The Eagles also have Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo up front on defense. Bradbury was acquired in an offseason trade with New England. He was flagged four times in the loss to the Vikings, two for holding and two for false starts.


Stats and stuff
— Philadelphia is 2-0 for the fourth time under coach Nick Sirianni. The Eagles won their first eight games in 2022 and their first five in 2023. They got off to a 4-0 start last season.


— The Eagles lead the NFL with a .705 (31-13) road winning percentage since the 2021 season.


— Philadelphia's defense surrendered 295 yards in Week 1 against Washington and 291 yards in Week 2 against Tennessee. It's the first time since 1995 that the Eagles held their opponents under 300 total yards in each of the first two games.


— Bears wide receiver Kalif Raymond leads the team with 13 catches through two games. He has six third-down receptions that have gone for first downs.


— Bears tight end Colston Loveland has one catch for 3 yards so far this year. He had a team-high 58 receptions for 713 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie last season.

stories.headline: Columbus Crew 2 fires Higuain after fallout from ref abuse
stories.summary: The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.
stories.body:
The Columbus Crew announced that Crew 2 manager Federico Higuain has been fired for cause, effective immediately, in the wake of his suspension by MLS NEXT Pro following an incident of misconduct towards a female referee.

"We determined it's in the best interest of our Club, players and support staff to dismiss Federico Higuaín from his responsibilities," said Crew General Manager Issa Tall in prepared statement. "After conversations this week and further assessing the past month, our Club's standards of what's expected from a leader for one of our teams have not been met," The Crew's statement added that for the 2026 MLS NEXT Pro Playoffs, the Crew 2 technical staff will assume additional responsibilities ahead of the Club's search for a full-time head coach for the side.

Higuain, 41, was suspended for two games following an Aug. 23 incident that involved him refusing to let go of the hand of a female referee during the post-game handshake, despite being asked three times to do so. Higuain also directed a sexist remark toward the referee saying: "Don't forget that this is a man's game."

Higuain, who excelled as a player for the Crew over eight seasons, was red carded for the incident. In addition to the two-game suspension, Higuain was ordered to undergo restorative practice training, sources told ESPN.

An MLS NEXT Pro spokesperson confirmed that Higuain was suspended for just one additional game, as the policy allows for the red card to count towards the total suspension. The same spokesperson wasn't able to answer the question of why Higuain's actions didn't constitute a forceful grab.

The Professional Soccer Referees Association (PSRA), the union that represents MLS and USL referees, brought the incident to light over the weekend, stating in a social media post that it was not satisfied with the penalties, adding that a "forceful grab" plus the discriminatory language should have been penalized more severely.

While the PSRA's post didn't mention Higuain by name, ESPN reported that the coach in question was Higuain.

"The League's response falls drastically short of the right message to the participants, the referees, and the public. It needs to be reevaluated," the PSRA's social media post read.

The Crew initially issued a statement stating that, "The Crew actively collaborated with MLS NEXT Pro throughout the review process and fully accepted the additional discipline issued in accordance with league policies.

"We condemn any action or notion that contradicts our mission of uniting and uplifting all communities and genders through the global game."

But sources with knowledge of the Crew's decision to fire its coach told ESPN that the club wasn't satisfied with Higuain's response to the incident, saying there was a "lack of contrition" on his part, that he refused to issue a public apology to the female referee, and that there was an overall lack of accountability on the part of its second-team coach.

There was pressure from several of the Crew's supporters groups as well, including the Nordecke and CapyBrava, which both made social media posts demanding that Higuain be fired.

One source said that Higuain was informed of the club's decision early Tuesday afternoon.

In a statement given to ESPN on Sunday, MLS NEXT Pro said the league "immediately investigated the reported incident between the head coach and the female official. It was determined that the coach's behavior violated League policies and warranted additional discipline beyond the red card that was issued in the moment. He served a two-game suspension and is required to participate in a multi-session restorative practices process, which is already underway. The program is intended to support the League's efforts to foster understanding, accountability, respect, and the restoration of relationships across the League. MLS NEXT Pro believes in the restorative approach. The League is confident in its process and the results."

stories.headline: Jaspa Fletcher outlines Lachie Neale legacy ahead of crucial call
stories.summary: Jaspa Fletcher will line up for his fourth AFL grand final in as many seasons aware he may never run out alongside Lachie Neale again.
stories.body:
Jaspa Fletcher has spelt out the impact Lachie Neale has made at the club as he grapples with the prospect of never playing alongside him for the Brisbane Lions again.

The 22-year-old will contest a fourth AFL grand final in his fourth season when the Lions face Fremantle on Saturday at the MCG.

As it stands Neale won't join him, the star midfielder on Thursday set to appeal a one-match suspension for striking that has ruled him out of the club's tilt for a third-straight title.

Two-time Brownlow Medallist Neale is widely tipped to join Collingwood next season.

"That's footy and that's business, and he's got to do what's right for him," Fletcher said of the former captain's likely move.

"But I'd love to still have him here, because as a mate and as a mentor as well, I can't thank him enough for what he's done for me.

"He's left such a great legacy at the club. I'm sure we'll keep a great connection over the journey."

Neale rates Fletcher, endorsing him among a host of capable young Lions leaders as a potential future captain.

"When I heard that, I was super honoured," Fletcher said.

"If that's the way the club wants to go, I'd be more than happy to do it.

"I'd do anything for the club."

Fletcher hasn't missed a game since his 2023 debut but admits his form, after preseason shoulder surgery, hadn't met his own expectations.

"I've been pretty honest ... I haven't been overly proud with how I've gone about it," he said.

"I could have got a little bit more out of myself, but that's behind me now and I've learnt a lot of lessons along the road, on and off the field."

And, after losing the only junior football grand final he reached "by 100 points", he hasn't taken his AFL career for granted.

"I'm just a product of being part of such a great club as such a great time," he said.

"In '23 we couldn't get it done, so to win a couple now is awesome. In 2023 you learn about how to go about the day, the week.

"As much as you want to win that, it set us up."

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings

Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.
